summary: Durable PICS promotion retries app 252190 because the current normalizer collapses repeated whitespace while an existing Tiger franchise row owns the exact raw name with a legacy noncanonical normalized_name. The writer only handles normalized_name conflicts, so PostgreSQL rejects the insert on the separate unique name constraint.
why_this_tier: Database correctness contributed +2, the external PICS worker contributed +1, and the isolated franchise write paths contributed -1. The database-correctness override required three independent read-only assessments.
observed_facts: At 2026-07-25T08:03:24.978925Z, primary work row 8176 for app 252190 was retrying at attempt 5/8 with PostgreSQL franchises_name_key collision evidence.
The conflicting persisted row is legacy.franchises.id 1669 with name and normalized_name both equal to the double-space form Defender's  Quest.
The current Python normalizer converts Defender's  Quest to the single-space value defender's quest.
App 252190 is already linked to franchise 1669, and franchise 1669 is shared by two apps.
Tiger enforces separate unique constraints on legacy.franchises.name and legacy.franchises.normalized_name.
Both Tiger franchise writer paths insert the raw name plus the current normalized value but handle only normalized_name conflicts.
At 2026-07-25T08:08:45.323155Z, Tiger had 14613 franchise rows, including 16 whose stored normalized_name differs from the current normalizer.
The same source-of-truth check found two groups, containing four rows, where distinct exact names collapse to the same current normalized value.
The 16 stale franchise rows are linked to 19 apps.
App 252190 remains PICS-pending and retryable; the failed promotion transaction did not partially delete its existing franchise relationship.
The targeted pre-fix PICS baseline passed 16 tests.
The shared exact-first resolver is covered in both durable promotion and Tiger latest-state relationship sync.
The post-fix targeted suite passed 22 tests and the complete PICS suite passed 108 tests.

reproduction_status.summary: Read-only Tiger evidence and the current normalizer reproduce the exact stale-normalization precondition: an exact raw-name owner exists under a legacy normalized value, while the writer attempts the same unique name under a different current normalized value.

db_checks.purpose: Verify the exact production retry, existing franchise identity, and existing app relationships.
db_checks.sql: SELECT id, appid, state, attempts, max_attempts, last_error_code, last_error_message FROM ops.pics_work_state WHERE id=8176 LIMIT 1; SELECT f.id, f.name, f.normalized_name, count(af.appid) FROM legacy.franchises f LEFT JOIN legacy.app_franchises af ON af.franchise_id=f.id WHERE f.id=1669 GROUP BY f.id, f.name, f.normalized_name LIMIT 1;
db_checks.result_summary: Work row 8176 was retrying at attempt 5/8 with an exact raw-name uniqueness error. Franchise 1669 owns that raw name under a legacy double-space normalized value and remains linked to two apps.

db_checks.purpose: Measure whether stale normalization and canonical collisions require a broader data repair.
db_checks.sql: SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE normalized_name <> regexp_replace(lower(btrim(name)), '[[:space:]]+', ' ', 'g')) FROM legacy.franchises; WITH canonical AS (SELECT regexp_replace(lower(btrim(name)), '[[:space:]]+', ' ', 'g') AS current_normalized FROM legacy.franchises), collisions AS (SELECT current_normalized, count(*) AS rows FROM canonical GROUP BY current_normalized HAVING count(*)>1) SELECT count(*), sum(rows) FROM collisions;
db_checks.result_summary: Tiger had 14613 franchise rows and 16 legacy noncanonical normalized values. Two canonical collision groups contain four rows: Dying Light/Dying  Light and Movavi Software/Movavi  Software. A mass data rewrite or silent merge would be unsafe and is outside this fix.

root_cause_hypotheses.label: The writer handles only normalized-name conflicts even though the table independently enforces unique raw names.
root_cause_hypotheses.evidence: The existing row owns the exact raw name under a legacy normalized value; the current code attempts that name under a new normalized value and PostgreSQL reports franchises_name_key rather than franchises_normalized_name_key.

root_cause_hypotheses.label: The PICS payload contains a malformed or incomplete association family.
root_cause_hypotheses.evidence: The source value matches the persisted raw franchise name exactly, the existing relationship is valid, and failure occurs only at uniqueness enforcement.

fix_options.title: Resolve existing raw or normalized identity before insert
fix_options.summary: Prefer an existing exact-name row, otherwise reuse the current-normalized row, and only insert when neither identity exists. Use targetless conflict handling plus a second lookup for concurrent inserts.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Preserves IDs and relationships and handles both unique constraints without schema or data migration. Adds bounded lookup statements to the small franchise relationship path.

fix_options.title: Canonicalize all stored normalized names
fix_options.summary: Rewrite legacy.franchises.normalized_name to the current Python normalization rule before processing.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Touches 8402 production rows, requires a separately approved migration and collision plan, and is unnecessary for safe idempotent ingestion.

fix_options.title: Catch the raw-name exception and retry by name
fix_options.summary: Keep the current insert and recover only after PostgreSQL raises a unique violation.
fix_options.tradeoffs: PostgreSQL aborts the current transaction after the error, so recovery would require savepoints or transaction restart and would be more fragile.

recommended_fix: Use one shared Tiger franchise resolver that selects exact name first, then current normalized_name; inserts with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING only when no row exists; and reselects after an insert race. Exact-name precedence preserves distinct legacy IDs in the two live canonical-collision groups. Reuse it in durable promotion and the Tiger latest-state path. Do not mutate existing names or normalized values.
